rows.title: Brown Rat
rows.attribution: (c) lucky, some rights reserved (CC BY)
rows.itemMetadataText:
So this rat could be talking to itself, or doing the rat equivalent of 'whistle while you work'. It's hard to hear considering the traffic, but it's kind of like the cartoony sound that a handsaw makes when you make it flap quickly back and forth (ask the Foley artist in your life). The sound is most audible at the beginning of the recording since it was casually walking away from my window. 

Was this a happy sound? I couldn't see if it was boggling as well (ask the pet rat guardian in your life what that is).

It may just be nonchalantly taunting us.

Second and better audio recording is here: https://www.inaturalist.ca/observations/135201463

AUDIO 
The chicks engage in constant chatter:

At the start of the recording there is a loud screech - the chick could no longer locate the adult male carer. 

Part way throught the recording there is a second slightly louder and different sound - this is one chick losing sight of the other chick.

When the male adult carer heard the first loud screech he immediately and silently moved in the direction of the sound. He did not react to the second sound.

The three constantly kept in touch, the chicks via sound, the adult via sight, never more than ten seconds from each other.

When the recording was played back to them they all became extremely agitated. The adult male immediately showed agressive indications.

Following this the adult male squatted down and the chicks hid under his body for a couple of minutes. Then they resumed chattter and looking for food.

Guides hoping to gain status with recordings should note this. It is not good practice.
